title: Attribute-driven access: SAML role mapping, KMS rotation & audit evidence checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket captures product requirements, scope clarifications, and the sign-off checklist for attribute-driven RBAC via SAML assertions, KMS/HSM key rotation policies, and audit log evidence required for Private deployments. The goal is to provide deterministic acceptance criteria for engineering, security, and customer onboarding teams so the feature can be validated in staging and production-like environments.
acceptance_criteria: SAML attribute mapping: customers can map SAML attributes (e.g., 'roles', 'group', 'eduPersonAffiliation') to Redwood RBAC roles via Console and via a declarative YAML mapping spec
Role precedence and conflict resolution behavior documented and implemented: when multiple attributes map to multiple roles, system picks union of permissions and honors explicit deny mappings
Minimum-privilege templates provided: at least three curated role templates (Viewer, Operator, Admin) with claim-to-role examples in Confluence
KMS integration: customer-managed KMS keys can be attached to Private clusters; keys support scheduled rotation and rotation can be initiated via Console, API, or automated schedule
HSM operator flow: where HSM-backed keys are used, documented procedures exist for key import/export (or lack thereof), operator responsibilities, and emergency key-rotation playbook

Audit logging: every SAML sign-in, role-assignment event, key-rotation event, and operator action is emitted to the configured audit sink with RFC3339 timestamps, UUID request IDs, and correlated user/principal IDs
Audit retention and export: audit logs stored for a minimum of 365 days in an immutable store and exportable to customer SIEM in JSONL with schema v1.2
Test harness: end-to-end test plan exists (SAML IdP emulator + KMS rotation simulator) and passes in staging for three distinct IdP providers (Okta, AzureAD, PingFederate)
Backwards compatibility: existing customers with prior RBAC mappings continue to work; migration tool provided for deprecated claim names
Operational observability: Console shows per-tenant last-auth timestamp, last-key-rotation timestamp, and a digest of recent audit events
signoff_checklist: Product: PRD approved and linked to this ticket
Security: Threat model & data flow reviewed (sec-0421 signoff)
Engineering: Feature branch merged and e2e tests green (GH PR #1429)
QA: Test matrix executed across three IdPs and KMS variants; results attached
Compliance: Audit schema validated and sample export ingested into Splunk/SIEM proof-of-concept
Docs: Console guidance + YAML mapping spec published in Confluence (Doc ID: conf/private-sso-rbac-2026)
Customer Ops: Runbook for emergency key rotation and operator contact list published
Legal: Data residency/retention sign-off for targeted regions (EU, US-East)
Release: Rollout plan with canary thresholds and fallback policy approved
decisions: Use attribute-based mapping (claims -> roles) rather than IdP-side role enforcement to keep audit surface uniform
Emit audit events in JSONL with explicit schema versioning to ease downstream parsing
Default retention set to 365 days for Private deployments; enterprise customers can request longer via support
For KMS rotation, support both scheduled automatic rotation and manual rotation initiated by operator; rotation events must produce verifiable audit entries
open_questions: Do we allow wildcard/group-to-role mappings for large orgs or require explicit lists? (impact on policy engine performance)
What level of proof is required from customers who request HSM import/export if their HSM provider forbids key export?
Should we support transient session-only keys for ephemeral workloads and how would that affect audit traceability?
